anchors.description: Vertical extent (top rail to bottom rail) of one raised-panel door on the four-door wood wall-cabinet bank above the right counter, a standard 30-36 in wall cabinet door.
anchors.visible_evidence: The wall cabinet bank shows four identical raised-panel doors; the marked segment runs down the centre of the second door face from just under the top rail to the bottom rail, both ends on the same cabinet front plane.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Wall cabinets may be 30 in (door about 25-27 in) or 36 in (door about 31-33 in); face-frame rail width shifts the door height within this range.

anchors.description: Width of one wall-cabinet door between the bank's outer left stile and the first centre mullion, standard 12-15 in door pitch.
anchors.visible_evidence: Along the same raised-panel door bank, the door pitch is uniform: left bank edge at the marked point and the next stile junction at the second marked point, both on the cabinet front plane.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Door widths in this style are commonly 12, 13 or 15 in; the stile-centre endpoints add about 0.5 in of frame on each side.

anchors.description: Outer rim diameter of the white ceramic coffee mug standing on the peninsula counter left of the faucet, measured across the widest horizontal chord of the rim.
anchors.visible_evidence: A white mug with a red logo sits on the dark granite peninsula counter beside the curved faucet; its rim ellipse is visible with clean left and right silhouette extremes.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: A standard 11 oz mug is about 3.25 in across the rim (0.083 m); a larger 15-16 oz mug would be near 0.10 m, so the interval covers both.
